questions.q: According to the AWS docs, where is Data Wrangler accessed in the newer Studio experience?
questions.explain: The docs say Data Wrangler has been integrated into SageMaker Canvas, and the newer Studio requires Canvas to access it. Older docs describe it as a Studio Classic feature.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of Data Wrangler's documented export destinations?
questions.explain: Documented export targets include S3, Feature Store, SageMaker Pipelines and a Python script.

questions.q: In the lesson's leakage screen, exit_survey_sent had a single-feature AUC of 0.989 while tenure_months had 0.617. What does this suggest?
options: exit_survey_sent is the best feature and should be kept
exit_survey_sent probably leaks the answer and should be reviewed
The dataset has no missing values
questions.explain: A column that almost perfectly separates the target on its own is suspicious. Here it was recorded after the churn decision, so it leaks.

questions.q: What happened to the test AUC when the leaky column was dropped in the lesson's run?
options: It fell from 0.991 to 0.632, which is the honest estimate
questions.explain: The model scored 0.991 with the leaky column and 0.632 without it. The lower number reflects what the model can do with information available at prediction time.

questions.q: Why export a Data Wrangler flow to a script or Pipelines step?
options: Exporting is required to open the flow
To make the preparation repeatable, the same way every time
To hide the steps from teammates
questions.explain: A flow that exists only as clicks is hard to reproduce. Exporting produces code that can run again on new data and be reviewed in Git.
